title: The built chat's team remembers decisions and preferences across chats, and no project write ever drops a memory note
request: Finish the Home team: data agent, reporter, project memory (the team remembers your decisions and preferences across chats), several tasks at once. Built memory first: the others read it.
spec: dclab_rnd/studio/memory.py (A5.2 notes: added or marked removed, never a cell value); the Home orchestrator (dclab_rnd/draft/orchestrator.py).
plan: Tools remember (write, move remember) and show_memory (read), owned by the Records reader.
The model reads the project's notes every turn (situation.remembered).
A note after each confirmed problem version, adopted improvement and built version.
Rules route explicit requests only; review; fix; agent-eval and harness-eval for the changed tool list.

decisions.decision: Notes are merged by id in the project stores (files and PostgreSQL), a removal winning, on every save and update.
decisions.why: Jobs save the whole project document after minutes; a note written meanwhile was dropped. One rule at the storage layer protects every writer, not only the chat.

decisions.decision: remember keeps the person's own words and refuses unless their message asked for it.
decisions.why: A model's paraphrase would be stored forever as the person's preference.

decisions.decision: Questions and changes of what is predicted or when are never preferences.
decisions.why: A changed prediction moment must go through the Problem analyst's check against the table, not sit in memory unchecked.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/orchestrator.py (remember, show_memory, notes after writes, routing), dclab_rnd/storage/notes.py (new), storage/postgres.py and studio/store.py (merge on save/update, a per-project lock in the file store), tests (home orchestrator, storage contract on both backends, model data limits)

findings.defect: Questions, complaints and moment changes became permanent preferences.
findings.scenario: "why do we always lose recall?", "from now on, predict at signup" routed to remember.
findings.cause: The first patterns matched any "we always/never" and "from now on".
findings.fix: asks_to_remember: never a question unless it starts with remember; never with a problem part or a prediction moment.

findings.defect: The model could store a note the person never asked for, labelled as the person's.
findings.scenario: "show the models, I don't care about recall today" and the model calls remember("we don't care about recall").
findings.cause: remember took the model's argument as it was.
findings.fix: remember refuses unless the person's message asks, and keeps their own redacted words.

findings.defect: Notes were lost or a removal undone by concurrent writes.
findings.scenario: A stage job reads the project, the person says remember, the job saves the whole document: the note is gone.
findings.cause: Every whole-document save replaced the memory list.
findings.fix: storage/notes.py merges notes by id on save and update in both backends; the chat's waiting list was removed.

findings.defect: A confirmed problem version was noted as "Problem changed" on a project that did not change.
findings.scenario: The intern on p1 reads it as a decision about p1's target.
findings.fix: "Version N of the problem confirmed", with the reason that this project still answers the problem it was built for.

findings.defect: The changed tool list needed the agent evaluations rerun.
findings.cause: Tool schemas are hashed like prompts.

findings.defect: The privacy check over every chat read tool counted the new one but saw no card.
findings.cause: The test project had no notes.
findings.fix: The test gives it one, so the memory card's content is checked too.

measurements.name: affected tests
measurements.result: home orchestrator 46, storage contract 25 on both backends, model data limits 35
limits: no live model run of remember yet

outcome: The team keeps decisions and preferences in the project's memory and every chat reads them; no write of the project can drop a note.
lessons: When many writers save whole documents, protect an append-only field where the document is written, not in each writer.
A tool that writes on the person's behalf must check the person's own words, not the model's.
risks: The file store's lock is per process: a separate worker process can still race; PostgreSQL locks the row.
A value the person types in their own sentence is kept (redaction removes emails and similar only).
